/-!
# Erdős Problem 749

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/749](https://www.erdosproblems.com/749)
-/

open Set Pointwise AdditiveCombinatorics

namespace Erdos749

/--
Let $\epsilon>0$. Does there exist $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$
such that the lower density of $A+A$ is at least $1-\epsilon$
and yet $1_A\ast 1_A(n) \ll_\epsilon 1$ for all $n$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_749 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ),
    ∃ A : Set ℕ, 1 - ε ≤ lowerDensity (A + A) ∧
    ((Nat.cast (R := ℝ) ∘ sumRep A) ≪ (fun n => (1: ℝ))) := by
  sorry


-- TODO(firsching): add a "similar question" for the upper density.
end Erdos749

reformulations.difference: Lean expresses bounded representation counts using `IsBigO atTop`, an eventual bound, whereas the source explicitly says the bound holds for all n.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every A ⊆ ℕ, sumRep A n counts ordered pairs summing to n and is at most n+1. If a bound C holds for n ≥ N, enlarging it to max(1, max(C,N)) also bounds every n < N. Conversely, a bound for all n implies the eventual big-O bound. The existential constant and set can be reordered inside the quantifier over ε, giving precisely a constant depending on ε. Review749.full_source_equivalence in /workspace/review/scratch.lean proves this equivalence without sorry or reliance on the conjecture.
